correctness.rationale: The source gives the six full-dimensional facet functions and normals. After Euclidean normalization, a radius-rho ball is feasible exactly under six linear clearance inequalities. Because every coefficient coupling the upper facets to s,t,v is nonnegative, lowering any feasible center coordinate to rho cannot hurt an upper clearance and only improves the top clearance. Thus feasibility is equivalent to feasibility at (rho,rho,rho), yielding the three displayed scalar upper bounds. Their minimum is attained, and the complete incenter set is exactly the same six normalized inequalities at the optimal radius.

value.rationale: The source prismatoids are the principal three-dimensional examples in a newly introduced family with rational linear precision, and their six facet functions are central to the paper's Horn-matrix analysis. The theorem gives a complete Euclidean Chebyshev profile across the whole positive six-facet parameter family: an exact inradius, a three-way tangency phase diagram, and every optimal center. This is a natural metric complement to the source's lattice/statistical structure rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
